stories.title: Victory for Soc Dems and Fine Gael in bye-elections
stories.summary: Counting is now complete in the two Dáil bye-elections with Fine Gael and the Social Democrats both winning one seat each this weekend. Fine Gael's Seán Kyne returns to the Dáil after securing President Catherine Connolly's old seat. It is a rare success for a Government party in a bye-election - and the first since 2014. Last night, Daniel Ennis of the Social Democrats took the Dublin Central seat vacated by former finance minister Paschal Donohoe. The bye-election results do not fundamentally alter the Dáil arithmetic.

stories.title: At a glance: The Dáil's two new TDs
stories.summary: So, who did the people of Dublin Central and Galway West send to the Dáil? Daniel Ennis is from Dublin's North Strand. He was a former League of Ireland footballer, operations manager in a shopping centre in Tallaght and volunteer with East Wall Bessborough Football Club before entering politics three years ago. The 38-year-old father of two says an "emotional shift" following the death of a friend and the birth of his second child prompted him to get involved in politics in 2023. He first worked in the constituency for TD Gary Gannon before becoming a councillor in 2024 after his first election run.

stories.title: Temperatures of up to 27C expected tomorrow
stories.summary: Met Éireann is forecasting "very warm" temperatures of up to 27C tomorrow, with "long spells of sunshine". It comes as the forecaster reported a temperature reading of 24.9C in the Phoenix Park in Dublin today. Met Éireann says it is provisionally the highest temperature of the year so far. Tomorrow is due to start with "mist and fog patches", but it will turn dry with plenty of sunshine.
